top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) is the best-attributed and most reproducible achievement on the slate: the magic-wavelength lattice idea is clean and checkable, the 1e-18 accuracy has been confirmed by independent laboratories over about two decades, and the many-atom regime goes beyond what the 2005 and 2012 prizes honoured. The two-name allocation is uncontested and the citation can be scoped to the lattice principle and its realization. P002 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) is a strong theory-then-experiment chain and my second choice, but the pairing mechanism is unsettled, sample variability is large, and the three-name limit leaves out Cao. A prize this year is preferable to none, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no personal or institutional tie to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, only a field-level interest in condensed-matter theory and many-body dynamics
